messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> INC-2026: high error-rate on service=ghost-inference-frontend ; routing_key=prod-routing ; urgency=high :rotating_light:

Sasha: getting the PD page now. PD shows service 'ghost-inference-frontend' — that name isn't in our prod services list.

Mike: I just got a page too. I was expecting inference-gateway-prod alerts. Could be a bad service alias or an old integration.

Jen: @Sasha @Mike backing up — what customer impact? Any 5xx spikes in realtime?

Oncall-SRE: Our metrics: 5m error-rate spike on /v1/generate aligns with alert. But origin tags show "cluster:dedicated-1" and service name ghost-inference-frontend.

Mike: Strange. CI deploy earlier renamed a canary service to ghost-inference for smoke tests but that should be non-prod. Wondering if a tag leaked into PD mapping.

Sasha: Paging PD console now — looks like there are two PD services with similar integration keys. One is `ghost-inference-frontend` (nonprod) and one `inference-gateway-prod`. Integration keys got swapped in the k8s secret for the routing-lambda.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-2026 acknowledged by Mike (@mike) :white_check_mark:

Mike: I'm on it. Reverted the k8s secret to the previous commit (kubectl apply -f -) — reloaded routing-lambda. Command used:
```bash
kubectl -n platform create secret generic pd-keys --from-literal=ROUTER_KEY=old-key-abc123 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n platform rollout restart deployment/routing-lambda
```

Jen: Nice. Are alerts still firing? Is PD auto-resolved?

incident-bot: PagerDuty update -> INC-2026: service changed to inference-gateway-prod ; status=acknowledged ; assigned_to=Mike

Oncall-SRE: After restart, inbound events are now labeled inference-gateway-prod. Error rates are slowly dropping, no new pages for the last 20s.

Sasha: Customer impact: we saw transient 20% increase in 5xxs for tenant=acme during the 2m window. Support ticket queued (SUP-4432). No persistent data loss.

Mike: Root cause timeline: 22:58 - smoke deploy created temporary service alias `ghost-inference` in staging; 22:59 - CI pipeline reused secret name `pd-keys` for staging job and inadvertently applied to prod routing-lambda because of ambiguous `--context` in pipeline. 23:00 - alerts routed to ghost-inference PD service.

Jen: Action items (quick):
- rotate the PD key used by staging so it cannot map to prod (owner: Mike, done)
- add pipeline guard to require explicit cluster context (owner: SRE, PR in flight)
- add a PD mapping validation to our infra tests so a non-prod service name cannot bind to prod routing (owner: Sasha)

Oncall-SRE: Will create mitigation runbook note: when PD pages show unfamiliar service names, check k8s secret revision and pipeline job contexts before escalating to oncall-rota.

Sasha: Filing a short postmortem draft. Will include timeline, impact (acme 2m 20% 5xx spike), root cause (secret/context reuse), and follow-ups.

Mike: FYI — no customer-facing escalation required beyond a note in support ticket. I'll attach logs and timeframe.

Jen: Thanks team. Closing PD incident after monitoring window. Please add your follow-up tasks to the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: INC-2026 resolved by Mike -> status=resolved ; duration=4m15s

Sasha: Postmortem owner assigned to Sasha. Will sync with Pipeline team tomorrow.

Oncall-SRE: Adding runbook PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/pd-routing-validation.md

Jen: Nice. We'll review in the SRE weekly. Good catch on the ambiguous context.

Sasha: Closing thread.
